research_domain_title: Government Capacity, Public Service, and Institutional Modernization
note: Defining institutional design doctrine. Architecture only — not a finished civil-service or IT statute. No invented statistics. Does not promise frictionless government without tradeoffs; commits to eliminating administrative waste while preserving or improving public service.

defining_design_question.constitutional_question: How do we build a government that delivers better outcomes with fewer layers, less friction, and greater accountability?

iconic_phrase.text: Government should become invisible—but never unaccountable.

meaning.invisible: Citizens should not notice bureaucracy because services work, forms are simple, approvals are fast, information flows, and agencies coordinate.
meaning.never_unaccountable: Every decision remains explainable, reviewable, measurable, auditable, and constitutionally limited.

role_in_philosophy: Neither shrink government until it cannot function, nor expand bureaucracy for its own sake. Build a lean constitutional government that is easy for citizens to use, hard to abuse, and constantly improving — expanding ordinary people’s capacity while keeping power transparent and accountable.

foundational_principle.text: Government work should be among the highest forms of civic service. Public institutions should use technology to eliminate unnecessary administrative labor so human talent can be concentrated in judgment, problem-solving, public engagement, oversight, and service.

friction_reduction_principle.text: Government should continuously reduce administrative friction while continuously improving public service.
friction_reduction_principle.clarification: Not reducing government as an end. Not reducing services as an end. Reducing friction — eliminating administrative waste while preserving or improving public service. Some regulations and oversight exist for legitimate reasons and are not treated as disposable.

operational_rule.text: Use technology to remove unnecessary bureaucracy, use human talent where judgment and compassion matter, and keep every public institution visible to the people who own it.

government_as_platform.summary: Government should operate as a coordinated platform behind one secure citizen portal so agencies communicate automatically; the citizen should not have to understand the organizational chart.

collect_once_principle.text: Collect once. Reuse securely with appropriate legal authorization.
collect_once_principle.summary: Bureaucracy often exists because of duplication. Multiple agencies repeatedly collect the same verified information. Privacy protections remain essential, but citizens should not repeatedly provide the same verified data without necessity.

value_chain_doctrine.wrong_question: How many employees can we eliminate?
value_chain_doctrine.right_question: What higher-value work should these employees be doing?

eighty_twenty_rule.note: Working design heuristic, not a measured universal statistic.
eighty_twenty_rule.routine_share_heuristic: A large share of government work is processing, routing, searching, copying, approvals, and compliance.
eighty_twenty_rule.judgment_share_heuristic: A smaller share requires judgment, ethics, negotiation, investigation, compassion, and constitutional interpretation.
eighty_twenty_rule.implication: Technology should focus on the routine category so humans can excel in the judgment category.

questions.text: Is government the proper institution to solve it?
What measurable benefit does it create?
What measurable cost does it create?
Does it expire automatically unless reviewed?

regulatory_workflow_rule.rejects: Crude one-in-two-out scoring as a complete design rule.
regulatory_workflow_rule.requires: Every new regulation should trigger review of the entire regulatory workflow.
regulatory_workflow_rule.design_question: Can we remove unnecessary steps while adding one necessary safeguard?

agency_value_rule: If an agency cannot explain what value it creates, it should be reviewed.

ai_in_government.rule: AI should never become the final decision-maker on matters affecting legal rights or significant benefits.
permitted_assistive_uses: drafting routine correspondence for human review
identifying potential fraud for human investigation
ai_in_government.final_judgment: Where legal rights or significant benefits are at stake, final judgment remains with accountable officials.

citizen_experience_metric.right_question: How easy was it for a citizen to accomplish their goal?
citizen_experience_metric.organization_rule: Government should be organized around life events, not agencies.

administrative_burden_innovation_require.summary: Every agency should continuously reduce administrative burden — not merely cut budget or headcount.
administrative_burden_innovation_require.reward: Solutions that remove friction while preserving or improving service.
administrative_burden_innovation_require.note: No fixed percentage mandate locked as finished policy; continuous burden reduction is the doctrine.

technology_doctrine.text: Automate the routine. Elevate the human.
technology_doctrine.guardrail: Technology must never become an excuse to remove access for people who are elderly, disabled, rural, poor, offline, or uncomfortable with digital systems. Every digital service should include a real human pathway.

arkansas_objective.text: Build a state government that is small enough to understand, capable enough to serve, transparent enough to trust, and open enough for ordinary citizens to enter and improve.
arkansas_objective.note: State model for testing; principles are portable. No fabricated Arkansas board counts or performance statistics.

professional_public_administration.summary: Long-term expertise roles (engineers, accountants, attorneys, public-health professionals, emergency managers, data specialists, auditors, planners, educators, infrastructure professionals) should not be forced out merely for making public service a career. Institutional knowledge matters.

civic_leadership.summary: Leadership and oversight positions should remain connected to ordinary civic life. Boards, commissions, advisory bodies, agency leadership, and policy roles should not become closed networks.

career_distinction.objective: Not eliminate career public servants; prevent career bureaucracy from becoming isolated from the public it serves.

appointment_evaluation_criteria: commitment to constitutional and ethical standards
appointment_rule: Political loyalty should not be the primary qualification.
citizen_visibility_question: What does this body do, who controls it, what did it decide, and how can I participate?

public_authority_inventory.name: Public Authority Inventory
review_questions: Should it be reformed, merged, sunset, or abolished?
public_authority_inventory.note: Design agenda — inventory not yet executed; do not invent entity counts.

sunset_and_renewal.rule: Every board, commission, agency program, and major administrative rule should have a review cycle. Not automatic expiration of everything, but periodic justification of existence, authority, budget, outcomes, structure, and public value.

civic_service_credential.name: Arkansas Civic Service Credential
civic_service_credential.note: Completion would not guarantee appointment; builds a larger qualified citizen pool. Not yet an operating program.

citizen_facing_account.summary: One secure government portal organized around the citizen, not agency silos — applications, licenses, fees, business registration, benefits, tax records, public requests, feedback, meetings, board applications, problem reports, case status, official records.
citizen_facing_account.rule: Citizens should not have to understand the organizational chart of government to receive a service.

agency_accountability_dashboard.rule: Not public relations. Show weaknesses alongside successes.

government_capacity_test.title: Constitutional Capitalism Government Capacity Test
government_capacity_test.purpose: Screen public-administration and modernization reforms before acceptance into the framework.

questions.text: Does it reduce administrative friction while preserving or improving public service?
Does technology automate routine work without removing human access pathways?
Does it elevate judgment, service, and oversight rather than only cutting payroll?
Does it organize around citizen life events rather than forcing citizens to navigate agency silos?
Does it collect information once and reuse it securely under lawful authorization?
Are boards, commissions, and appointments visible, open, and periodically reviewable?
Does it publish honest performance — including failures — not only successes?
If AI is used, does final judgment on legal rights or significant benefits remain with accountable officials?
Does it preserve rural, offline, elderly, disabled, and low-income access?
Does it make government easier to use for citizens while remaining harder to abuse and continuously improvable?

research_status.next: Phase 2.1: register primary sources for state boards inventories, digital-service standards, civil-service systems; begin Arkansas Public Authority Inventory structure without inventing counts
